# Android Project Rules for Gemini AI
## Project Overview This project follows modern Android development best practices using Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Clean Architecture (MVVM). The rules below provide guidance for maintaining consistent architecture and code quality across any Android application.
## Architecture Principles
### Clean Architecture Layers The project follows strict Clean Architecture with three distinct layers:
1. **Data Layer** (`data/`) - Room database entities in `data/local/entity/` - DAOs in `data/local/dao/` - Repository implementations in `data/repository/` - Never expose entities or DTOs to UI layer
2. **Domain Layer** (`domain/`) - Pure Kotlin - NO Android dependencies - Domain models in `domain/model/` - Repository interfaces in `domain/repository/` - Use cases in `domain/usecase/` - Services in `domain/service/` - DTOs in `domain/model/dto/`
3. **UI Layer** (`ui/`) - ViewModels in `ui/viewmodel/` - Screens in `ui/screens/` (or `ui/` subdirectories) - Compose components in `ui/components/` - Navigation in `ui/navigation/`
### Strict Separation Rules - **NEVER** import Android classes in the domain layer - **NEVER** expose Room entities to the UI layer - always map to domain models - **NEVER** put business logic in ViewModels or Composables - use UseCases - **NEVER** access Context in repositories - use dependency injection - **ALWAYS** use immutable data classes for UI state - **ALWAYS** expose immutable StateFlow from ViewModels (use `.asStateFlow()`)
## Code Style & Patterns
### ViewModels - Use Unidirectional Data Flow (UDF) - Expose single `StateFlow<UiState>` for screen state - Use `SavedStateHandle` for process death handling - Keep ViewModels thin - delegate logic to UseCases - Example pattern: ```kotlin class ExampleViewModel( private val useCase: SomeUseCase, private val savedStateHandle: SavedStateHandle ) : ViewModel() { private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(ExampleUiState()) val uiState: StateFlow<ExampleUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()
fun onEvent(event: ExampleEvent) { when (event) { is ExampleEvent.SomeAction -> handleAction() } } } ```
### Use Cases - Single responsibility - one use case = one action - Use `operator fun invoke()` pattern - Keep business logic here, not in ViewModels - Example pattern: ```kotlin class GetItemsUseCase( private val repository: ItemRepository ) { operator fun invoke(params: GetItemsParams): Flow<List<Item>> { return repository.getItems(params) } } ```
### Repositories - Interface in domain layer, implementation in data layer - Use Flow for reactive data streams - Handle offline-first logic (local cache priority) - Map entities to domain models internally
### Database Operations - Use Room transactions for multi-table operations - Use `@Transaction` annotation for complex operations - Ensure data consistency when updating related entities - Example: `insertWithRelatedEntityUpdate()`
## Data Types & Precision
### Numeric Values - Use `BigDecimal` for monetary or precise decimal values - Use appropriate scale for intermediate calculations - Round to user-specified precision at display time - Consider using `Double` for simple numeric values where precision is not critical
### Timestamps - Store timestamps as `Long` (UTC milliseconds) - Use proper timezone handling when displaying - Consider using `Instant` or `LocalDateTime` from java.time for complex date operations
## Domain Models
### General Guidelines - Use data classes for models that need equality checks - Primary keys: Use `Long` with autoGenerate for auto-incrementing, or `String` (UUID) for business keys - Include only relevant fields - avoid over-modeling - Use sealed classes for restricted hierarchies (e.g., state types, result types)
## Services
### Service Layer Purpose - Services contain business logic that spans multiple use cases - Services should be stateless and reusable - Examples: Analytics computation, data transformation, complex business rules - Services can be injected into use cases or viewmodels
## Concurrency & Threading
- Use `Dispatchers.IO` for database and network operations - Use `Dispatchers.Default` for CPU-intensive calculations - Use `Dispatchers.Main` only for UI updates - Use `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` in Compose for Flow collection
## Dependency Injection
- Use constructor injection (Hilt or Koin) - Never create dependencies manually in classes - Scope repositories and DAOs as singletons - Inject UseCases into ViewModels
## Anti-Patterns to Avoid
❌ **DO NOT**: - Put business logic in Composables - Expose MutableStateFlow from ViewModels - Pass Context to repositories - Use hardcoded magic strings - Block the main thread with database queries - Create "God" ViewModels with hundreds of lines - Neglect process death handling - Access Android APIs in domain layer
✅ **DO**: - Use UseCases for business logic - Expose immutable StateFlow - Use DI for all dependencies - Use const val or sealed classes for constants - Use coroutines/Flow properly - Keep ViewModels focused on UI state - Use SavedStateHandle for critical state - Keep domain layer pure Kotlin
## File Naming Conventions
- ViewModels: `[Feature]ViewModel.kt` - Screens: `[Feature]Screen.kt` - Use Cases: `[Action]UseCase.kt` - Repositories: `[Entity]Repository.kt` (interface in domain, impl in data) - Entities: `[Entity]Entity.kt` (data layer) - Domain Models: `[Model].kt` (domain layer) - DTOs: `[Purpose]DTO.kt` (domain/model/dto/)
## Testing Guidelines
- Domain layer should be fully testable without Android dependencies - Use fake repositories for ViewModel testing - Test UseCases independently - Test UI state transitions in ViewModels
## Documentation References
When making changes, refer to project-specific documentation: - Architecture documentation in `docs/architecture/` - Best practices in `docs/guidelines/` - Implementation guides in `docs/implementation/`

# Android Architecture Rules for Gemini AI
## Layer-Specific Rules
### Data Layer (`data/`)
#### Entity Rules - All entities must use Room annotations (`@Entity`, `@PrimaryKey`, etc.) - Primary keys: Use `Long` with autoGenerate for auto-incrementing IDs, or `String` (UUID) for business keys - Use appropriate data types based on field requirements (BigDecimal for precision, Long or Instant for timestamps, etc.) - Timestamps: Store as `Long` (UTC milliseconds) - Relationships: Use foreign keys with proper cascade actions - Soft delete: Include `isArchived` or similar boolean fields where applicable
#### DAO Rules - Use `@Query` with Room SQL for complex queries - Return `Flow<List<T>>` for reactive data streams - Use `@Transaction` for multi-table operations - Include sync versions of queries (non-Flow) when needed for one-time operations - Example: `getAllItems()` returns Flow, `getAllItemsSync()` returns List
#### Repository Implementation Rules - Implement repository interfaces from domain layer - Map entities to domain models internally (never expose entities) - Handle offline-first logic: check local cache first, then remote - Use appropriate dispatchers: `Dispatchers.IO` for database operations - Inject DAOs and remote data sources via constructor
### Domain Layer (`domain/`)
#### Strict No-Android Rule - **ZERO Android imports allowed** in domain layer - No Context, no Activity/Fragment, no View, no AndroidX classes - Pure Kotlin only - makes domain layer testable and platform-independent - If you need Android-specific functionality, move it to data or UI layer
#### Domain Model Rules - Use immutable data classes - No Room annotations or database-specific logic - Use appropriate data types based on domain requirements - Timestamps: `Long` - Include computed properties where useful (e.g., calculated totals, derived status)
#### Repository Interface Rules - Define interfaces in domain layer - Return Flow for reactive streams - Use suspend functions for one-time operations - Keep interfaces clean - no implementation details
#### Use Case Rules - Single responsibility principle: one use case = one business action - Use `operator fun invoke()` pattern for clean call syntax - Accept domain models as parameters, return domain models or Flow - Contain business logic, calculations, and data transformations - Example: `GetFilteredItemsUseCase`, `CalculateTotalsUseCase`
#### Service Rules - For complex business logic that spans multiple use cases - Stateless classes with pure functions - Examples: AnalyticsService, DataTransformationService, BusinessLogicService - Services can be injected into use cases or viewmodels
#### DTO Rules - Use DTOs in `domain/model/dto/` for data transfer between layers - Example: ItemRequest for creating/updating items - Example: ItemPrefillDTO for UI prefilling - Keep DTOs focused on specific use cases
### UI Layer (`ui/`)
#### ViewModel Rules - Extend `ViewModel()` from AndroidX - Use `SavedStateHandle` for process death survival - Expose immutable StateFlow using `.asStateFlow()` - Use Unidirectional Data Flow pattern - Keep thin - delegate to use cases - Handle UI events in `onEvent()` methods - Use appropriate dispatchers for different operations
#### Screen Rules - Use Jetpack Compose for all UI - Screen functions should be `@Composable` - Collect state using `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` - Keep composables focused on UI rendering only - Pass lambdas for user actions to ViewModel - Use proper state hoisting
#### Component Rules - Create reusable components in `ui/components/` - Keep components small and focused - Use parameters for customization, not hardcoded values - Follow Compose best practices (no side effects, proper state management)
#### Navigation Rules - Use Compose Navigation - Define routes as constants or sealed classes - Pass navigation callbacks to ViewModels - Handle back stack properly
## Data Flow Patterns
### Data Creation Flow 1. UI collects input → creates `ItemRequest` DTO 2. ViewModel calls `addItem(request)` 3. Use case validates and processes 4. Repository maps to entity and inserts 5. DAO uses transaction to update related entities 6. Flow updates trigger UI recomposition
### Analytics/Computation Flow 1. ViewModel provides `Config` 2. ViewModel calls appropriate service method (e.g., `AnalyticsService.computeMetrics`) 3. Service filters data by config.filter 4. Service applies transformations using other services 5. Service aggregates and computes results 6. UI renders via appropriate component
### Filter Application Flow 1. User modifies filter in UI 2. ViewModel updates `filter` StateFlow 3. Use case observes filter changes 4. Repository builds SQL query or applies in-memory filtering 5. Results flow back to UI
## Dependency Rules
### Allowed Dependencies by Layer
**Data Layer can depend on:** - Domain layer (interfaces, models) - Android/Room libraries - Network libraries (Retrofit, etc.) - Kotlin stdlib and coroutines
**Domain Layer can depend on:** - Kotlin stdlib - Kotlin coroutines - Java BigDecimal - NOTHING else (especially no Android)
**UI Layer can depend on:** - Domain layer (models, use cases, repository interfaces) - AndroidX libraries (Compose, Navigation, ViewModel, etc.) - Kotlin stdlib and coroutines
### Dependency Injection - Use constructor injection exclusively - Define dependencies in DI module (Hilt/Koin) - Scope repositories and DAOs as singletons - Scope ViewModels to navigation or activity lifecycle - Never use `object` or static access for dependencies
## Common Patterns
### Repository Pattern ```kotlin // Domain layer interface ItemRepository { fun getItems(params: GetParams): Flow<List<Item>> suspend fun saveItem(item: Item) }
// Data layer class ItemRepositoryImpl( private val itemDao: ItemDao ) : ItemRepository { override fun getItems(params: GetParams): Flow<List<Item>> { return itemDao.getAllItems(params).map { entities -> entities.map { it.toDomain() } } } } ```
### Use Case Pattern ```kotlin class GetItemsUseCase( private val repository: ItemRepository ) { operator fun invoke(params: GetParams, filter: Filter): Flow<List<Item>> { return repository.getFilteredItems(params, filter) } } ```
### ViewModel Pattern ```kotlin class ItemViewModel( private val getItems: GetItemsUseCase, private val savedStateHandle: SavedStateHandle ) : ViewModel() { private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(ItemUiState()) val uiState: StateFlow<ItemUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()
fun onEvent(event: ItemEvent) { when (event) { is ItemEvent.LoadItems -> loadItems() } }
private fun loadItems() { viewModelScope.launch { getItems(params, filter).collect { items -> _uiState.update { it.copy(items = items) } } } } } ```
## Architecture Violations to Detect
### Critical Violations - Android imports in domain layer - Room entities exposed to UI layer - Mutable StateFlow exposed from ViewModel - Context passed to repository - Business logic in Composable functions - Blocking operations on main thread
### Warning Violations - Use cases with multiple responsibilities - ViewModels with excessive business logic - Direct database access from UI layer - Hardcoded strings or magic numbers - Missing process death handling
## File Organization
### Package Structure ``` com.example.app/ ├── data/ │ ├── local/ │ │ ├── entity/ # Room entities │ │ ├── dao/ # Room DAOs │ │ └── database/ # Room database setup │ ├── remote/ # API interfaces (if applicable) │ └── repository/ # Repository implementations ├── domain/ │ ├── model/ # Domain models │ ├── model/dto/ # Data transfer objects │ ├── repository/ # Repository interfaces │ ├── usecase/ # Use cases │ └── service/ # Business logic services └── ui/ ├── viewmodel/ # ViewModels ├── screens/ # Screen composables ├── components/ # Reusable components ├── navigation/ # Navigation setup └── theme/ # Theme, colors, typography ```
## Testing Architecture
### Unit Tests - Domain layer: Test use cases and services with fake repositories - Data layer: Test repository implementations with in-memory database - UI layer: Test ViewModels with fake use cases
### Integration Tests - Test repository with real database - Test use case chains - Test complete flows (e.g., item creation, data processing)
### UI Tests - Test Compose components - Test screen navigation - Test user interactions

# Kotlin & Android Coding Standards for Android
## Kotlin Language Standards
### Naming Conventions
**Classes/Interfaces:** - PascalCase: `ItemRepository`, `ItemViewModel`, `DataService`
**Functions/Properties:** - camelCase: `getItems()`, `insertItem()`, `calculateTotals`
**Constants:** - UPPER_SNAKE_CASE or PascalCase for object properties: ```kotlin const val DEFAULT_VALUE = "default" object Constants { val MAX_ITEMS = 100 } ```
**Private properties:** - Prefix with underscore for backing properties: `_uiState`, `_transactions`
### Code Style
**Data Classes:** - Use `data class` for models that need `equals()`, `hashCode()`, `copy()` - Use `value class` for wrapping single values (when needed for performance) - Keep data classes immutable (`val` only)
**Sealed Classes:** - Use for restricted class hierarchies - Example: `Filter`, `Range`, `ItemType` - Enable exhaustive `when` expressions
**Extension Functions:** - Use for utility functions that extend existing classes - Place in files named like `*.extensions.kt` - Example: `BigDecimal.toFormattedString()`
**Null Safety:** - Avoid nullable types when possible - Use `?` only when null is a valid state - Use `!!` sparingly and only when you're certain - Prefer `requireNotNull()` or `checkNotNull()` for validation
### Coroutines & Flow
**Dispatchers:** - `Dispatchers.IO` for database and network operations - `Dispatchers.Default` for CPU-intensive calculations - `Dispatchers.Main.immediate` for UI updates in ViewModels - Never use `Dispatchers.Main` for blocking operations
**Flow Collection:** - Use `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` in Compose - Use `viewModelScope.launch` for collecting in ViewModels - Use `flow { }` builder for creating flows - Use operators like `map`, `filter`, `combine` for transformations
**StateFlow vs SharedFlow:** - Use `StateFlow` for single source of truth state - Use `SharedFlow` for events (one-time occurrences) - Always expose `StateFlow` as immutable using `.asStateFlow()`
**Coroutine Scope:** - Use `viewModelScope` in ViewModels (auto-cancels on ViewModel clear) - Use `lifecycleScope` in Activities/Fragments (auto-cancels on lifecycle) - Use `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO)` for background work
### Collections
**List vs Sequence:** - Use `List` for small collections or when you need random access - Use `Sequence` for large collections or chained operations to avoid intermediate allocations
**Immutable Collections:** - Prefer `List`, `Set`, `Map` over mutable variants - Use `toList()`, `toSet()`, `toMap()` to create immutable copies - Use `buildList`, `buildSet` for building mutable collections then converting
**Collection Operations:** - Use functional operators: `map`, `filter`, `flatMap`, `reduce`, `fold` - Use `associateBy`, `groupBy` for transformations - Use `distinct`, `distinctBy` for removing duplicates
## Android-Specific Standards
### Jetpack Compose
**Composable Functions:** - Prefix with `@Composable` - Use PascalCase for composable names - Keep functions small and focused - Avoid side effects in composable bodies
**State Management:** - Use `remember` for local state - Use `rememberSaveable` for state that survives process death - Use `mutableStateOf` for mutable state - Use `derivedStateOf` for computed state - Hoist state to the lowest common ancestor
**Side Effects:** - Use `LaunchedEffect` for one-time effects - Use `rememberCoroutineScope` for coroutine scopes in composables - Use `SideEffect` for effects that need to execute on every recomposition - Use `DisposableEffect` for cleanup
**Modifiers:** - Chain modifiers in order of specificity - Use standard modifiers before custom ones - Example: `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp).clickable { }`
**Preview:** - Use `@Preview` annotation for composable previews - Create multiple previews for different states - Use `@PreviewParameter` for parameterized previews
### Room Database
**Entity Definitions:** - Use `@Entity` with `tableName` for custom table names - Use `@PrimaryKey` with `autoGenerate = true` for auto-incrementing IDs - Use `@ColumnInfo` for custom column names - Use `@Ignore` for fields that shouldn't be stored - Use `@Embedded` for nested objects - Use `@Relation` for relationships
**Type Converters:** - Create converters for non-standard types (BigDecimal, Date, enums) - Use `@TypeConverters` annotation on entities, DAOs, or database - Example: `BigDecimalConverter`, `RangeConverter`
**DAO Queries:** - Use `@Query` with SQL for complex queries - Use parameter binding: `:paramName` - Use `@Transaction` for multi-table operations - Return `Flow` for reactive queries - Use `suspend` for insert/update/delete operations
**Database Migration:** - Use `Migration` class for schema changes - Test migrations with `MigrationTestHelper` - Use fallback to destructive migration only in debug builds
### Dependency Injection (Hilt)
**Module Setup:** - Create modules in `di/` package - Use `@Module` and `@InstallIn` annotations - Use `@Provides` for providing dependencies - Use `@Binds` for interface implementations
**Scoping:** - Use `@Singleton` for application-wide dependencies - Use `@ViewModelScoped` for ViewModels - Use `@ActivityScoped` for Activity-specific dependencies - Use custom scopes for feature-specific dependencies
**Injection Points:** - Use `@Inject constructor` for class injection - Use `@AndroidEntryPoint` for Activities, Fragments, ViewModels - Use `@HiltViewModel` for ViewModels - Use `@Inject` for field injection (rarely needed)
### ViewModels
**Lifecycle:** - Extend `ViewModel()` from AndroidX - Use `viewModelScope` for coroutines (auto-cancels) - Use `SavedStateHandle` for process death survival - Clean up resources in `onCleared()` override
**State Management:** - Use `MutableStateFlow` for mutable state - Expose as immutable `StateFlow` using `.asStateFlow()` - Use single `UiState` data class when possible - Use `update { }` extension for updating immutable state
**Event Handling:** - Use sealed classes for events - Handle events in `onEvent()` method - Use `SharedFlow` for one-time events (navigation, toasts)
### Navigation
**Compose Navigation:** - Use `NavHost` with `navController` - Define routes as constants or sealed classes - Use `navController.navigate()` for navigation - Use `navController.popBackStack()` for back navigation - Pass arguments as part of route or in `NavOptions`
**Type-Safe Navigation:** - Consider using type-safe navigation libraries - Define navigation models for type safety - Use sealed classes for route definitions
## Performance Standards
### Memory Management
**Avoid Memory Leaks:** - Never hold references to Activities/Contexts in singletons - Use weak references when necessary - Clear references in `onCleared()` or lifecycle callbacks - Use `viewLifecycleOwner` in Fragments instead of `this`
**Object Allocation:** - Reuse objects when possible (e.g., Paint, Path) - Use object pools for frequently created objects - Avoid object allocation in hot paths (draw loops, scroll)
**Lazy Initialization:** - Use `by lazy` for deferred initialization - Use `lateinit` for properties that will be initialized before use - Consider `lazy` for expensive computations
### Database Performance
**Query Optimization:** - Use indexes on frequently queried columns - Avoid `SELECT *` - select only needed columns - Use `@Query` with proper WHERE clauses - Consider pagination for large datasets
**Transaction Usage:** - Use `@Transaction` for multi-table operations - Batch inserts/updates when possible - Avoid nested transactions
### UI Performance
**Compose Performance:** - Use `remember` to avoid recomputation - Use `key()` in lists to stabilize item identity - Avoid expensive operations in composable bodies - Use `derivedStateOf` for computed state that depends on multiple states
**RecyclerView/Lists:** - Use proper `DiffUtil` implementations - Implement view holders efficiently - Avoid complex layouts in list items
## Testing Standards
### Unit Tests
**Structure:** - Use Given-When-Then pattern in test names - Use descriptive test names - Arrange-Act-Assert pattern in test bodies - Use `@Before` and `@After` for setup/teardown
**Mocking:** - Use MockK for mocking - Mock external dependencies (repositories, services) - Don't mock data classes or simple objects - Test behavior, not implementation details
**Coroutines Testing:** - Use `runTest` for coroutine tests - Use `TestDispatcher` for controlling coroutine execution - Use `advanceUntilIdle()` to wait for async operations
### Instrumented Tests
**Room Testing:** - Use `inMemoryDatabaseBuilder` for fast tests - Use `MigrationTestHelper` for migration tests - Test DAO methods independently
**UI Testing:** - Use Compose Testing for UI tests - Use `composeTestRule` for test assertions - Test user interactions and state changes - Use semantic tags for component identification
## Security Standards
### Data Security
**Encryption:** - Use EncryptedSharedPreferences for sensitive data - Use EncryptedFile for sensitive files - Use Android Keystore for cryptographic operations
**Network Security:** - Use HTTPS for all network calls - Use certificate pinning for critical APIs - Validate and sanitize all inputs
### Permission Handling
**Runtime Permissions:** - Request permissions at runtime - Handle permission denials gracefully - Explain why permissions are needed - Use ActivityResultContracts for permissions
## Code Quality
### Code Organization
**File Length:** - Keep files under 300 lines when possible - Split large classes into multiple files if needed - Use `private` functions to reduce complexity
**Function Length:** - Keep functions under 50 lines - Extract complex logic into separate functions - Use descriptive function names
**Complexity:** - Avoid deep nesting (max 3-4 levels) - Use early returns to reduce nesting - Extract complex conditions to named functions
### Documentation
**KDoc:** - Document public APIs with KDoc - Use `@param` for parameters - Use `@return` for return values - Use `@throws` for exceptions
**Comments:** - Use comments to explain WHY, not WHAT - Avoid obvious comments - Keep comments up to date with code
### Error Handling
**Exceptions:** - Use specific exception types - Catch exceptions at appropriate levels - Never catch `Exception` or `Throwable` broadly - Use `Result` type for operations that can fail
**Logging:** - Use Timber for logging - Use appropriate log levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) - Don't log sensitive information - Remove or disable debug logs in production
## Build Configuration
### Gradle
**Dependencies:** - Use version catalog (libs.versions.toml) - Keep dependencies up to date - Use stable versions in production - Document why specific versions are pinned
**Build Variants:** - Use debug and release variants - Configure ProGuard/R8 for release builds - Use different configurations for different variants
**Code Quality Tools:** - Enable detekt for static analysis - Enable ktlint for code formatting - Configure Android Lint checks - Use strict compilation checks
